text:
jon: Heads-up: we need a follow-up on the precision shim deprecation. Ops wants a single bridge that can speak FP8/INT8/4-bit without forcing customers to change. Quick brainstorming thread.

anya: Keep the bridge as a thin compatibility layer. Responsibilities: profile selection, device capability probing, fallback ordering, and telemetry tagging. No API breaking changes.

kevin: Important: different quant formats have distinct failure modes. Bridge must surface a per-endpoint precision_profile override so we can tune by workload.

maria: Example override payload idea?

kevin: {"endpoint":"embed-v2","precision_profile":"safe-int8-first","quality_budget":"0.995","fallback_order":"[\"int8\",\"fp8\",\"4bit\"]","telemetry_tag":"quant-bridge-1"}

luke: Ops constraint: fallback ordering cannot be static; it must be adjusted per-GPU via a device capability probe at node init and cached. Some kernels perform fp8 faster than int8.

jon: Agreed. Also need a KV-cache warm/invalidate strategy when switching precision to avoid subtle tokenization cache mismatches.

anya: Rollout proposal: (1) shadow mode on a small set of endpoints, (2) soft-fallback server-side opt-in, (3) customer canary + opt-in, (4) full enable and shim removal.

maria: Telemetry fields to add: model_id, precision_used, fallback_reason, degradation_score, latency_delta, tokens_served. Make them queryable in Console.

ops-bot: CI: shadow-integration passed on ampere and intel nodes, quant-bias test failed on older t4 images. See /ci/quant/1287.

kevin: For T4s we should tighten fallback thresholds or add a GPU-profile whitelist. I'll add per-gpu-profile heuristics.

jon: Policy question: should customers be allowed to force a precision (force_int8)? I think yes but only with admin opt-in and warnings; allow an auto-fallback safety-net if degradation_score exceeds threshold.

anya: Expose force_precision in endpoint settings and require admin approval. Log and surface fallback telemetry for compliance.

luke: SDK change: add optional precision_preference in client options; default null. Server honors, but auto-fallback occurs unless customer sets allow_auto_fallback=false (enterprise only).

maria: Docs: update api/precision.md and add migration guide + explanation of degradation_score semantics. I'll start a PR.

kevin: Dev tasks: implement bridge core, device probe, per-gpu whitelist, hysteresis params, telemetry schema.

jon: Proposed timeline: 2w for bridge core + probe, 1w for shadow telemetry validation, 2w for canary + customer comms, 4w for gradual shim removal = ~9w. Can parallelize docs + SDK + telemetry pipeline.

anya: Sounds doable. Schedule follow-up after shadow telemetry in 7 days. :calendar:

ops-bot: Action created: quant-bridge/EPIC-42, canary tag quant-bridge/canary added to release checklist.
